writing.prompt: Explain how a trait can show continuous variation rather than a simple 3:1 pattern.
writing.model: Multiple genes can contribute different effects, and environmental conditions can influence expression and development. Many combinations produce a range of measurements. A single complete-dominance Punnett square is therefore not an adequate model for every trait.
criteria: Identifies the relevant structures or quantities.
Explains the causal relationship or calculation, not just the final result.
Uses the stated evidence and avoids a stronger conclusion than it supports.

writing.prompt: Distinguish a change in gene expression from a change in DNA sequence.
writing.model: A gene-expression change affects how genetic information is used or how much product is produced. The allele sequence can remain unchanged. A mutation changes the DNA sequence itself. Either can influence phenotype, but they are not the same process.
criteria: Identifies the relevant structures or quantities.

videos.title: Polygenic traits and environmental influences — video support
videos.purpose: Explain polygenic and environmental contributions, and distinguish genotype, gene expression and measured phenotype.
videos.fallback: Nutrition, temperature and other conditions can influence a phenotype. Plants with similar genotypes may reach different heights under different light or nutrient conditions. The measured difference does not automatically establish a difference in DNA sequence. Gene expression describes which genetic information is used and how much product is made. Cells with the same inherited genome can have different functions because they express different sets of genes. Environmental or developmental signals can change expression. Some regulatory changes involve chemical modifications associated with DNA or chromatin. These are often discussed as epigenetic changes. Do not treat every such change as a mutation or assume it is always inherited through many generations.

worked.title: Interpret an environmental comparison
worked.scenario: Genetically similar cuttings are grown under high or low light, with other measured conditions kept similar. Their average growth differs.
steps: The genetic similarity reduces one source of variation.
The light condition differs systematically, so it is a plausible contributor.
The result concerns growth under those conditions; it does not prove a new allele appeared.
Check replication and other controlled conditions before making a stronger causal claim.
